verdict.rationale: Buzz gives agents their own Nostr keypairs as scoped credentials for channel membership, reading history, and posting messages, with NIP-98/NIP-42 signed-event auth replacing tokens, plus a CLI and ACP harness that let agents read (@mentions, search) and post via this identity model. Evidence spans first-party docs (buzz-gh-4, buzz-supp-acp-harness, buzz-supp-nip-aa-agent-auth, buzz-supp-nostr-open-protocol) and probes confirming these docs are live. missing for 10: no independent/hands-on confirmation of an agent actually posting via the API in production, and no traditional 'official API' with bearer tokens (auth uses signed Nostr events rather than conventional scoped tokens, requiring interpretation).
